options.label: Solid
options.meaning: Uses solid-style fibre filling along the configured guide directions, rather than an open cellular rib pattern. It does not prove a void-free printed composite.

options.label: Rhombic grid
options.meaning: Uses two configured rib directions to form a diamond-like fibre network. The two angles control its directional layout.

options.label: Isogrid
options.meaning: Uses an isogrid-style triangular rib network. Its guide angle and density set orientation and spacing; no structural rating is implied.

options.label: Anisogrid
options.meaning: Uses a directionally arranged rib network with adjustable main-rib angles and crossing placement. It allows an intentionally unequal directional layout.

options.label: Tetragrid
options.meaning: Uses the named multi-rib grid with separate main-rib and side-slope angle controls. Preview those ribs together; the label alone does not define a tested layup.

options.label: Line
options.meaning: Parallel straight fill paths. A simple directional fill; spacing and angle determine coverage.

options.label: Grid
options.meaning: Crossing line families forming a grid. This gives connections in more than one direction but creates intersections.

options.label: Triangles
options.meaning: Three-direction line families forming triangular cells. Intersections and orientation affect the resulting structure and print behavior.

options.label: Zigzag
options.meaning: Back-and-forth fill joined where the geometry permits. It reduces separate line starts compared with disconnected lines.

options.label: Concentric
options.meaning: Nested paths following the region's outline. Useful when following contours matters; inspect narrow centers and corners.

options.label: Honeycomb
options.meaning: A cellular pattern based on hexagonal cells. It creates repeated cell walls rather than long parallel fill lines.

options.label: Tri-Hexagon
options.meaning: A pattern combining triangular and hexagonal regions. It changes cell geometry compared with a simple grid or honeycomb.

options.label: Gyroid
options.meaning: A smoothly varying three-dimensional periodic infill pattern. Layer shapes change through the height rather than repeating one flat grid.

options.label: 3D Honeycomb
options.meaning: A honeycomb-style cellular structure that changes through the height. Inspect successive layers rather than judging it from one layer.

options.label: Cubic
options.meaning: A three-dimensional, cube-derived lattice. Its cross-section changes with height and distributes paths across several directions.

options.label: Crosshatch
options.meaning: A crossing-line hatch pattern. It changes the line arrangement and junction layout; compare the actual paths with Grid before choosing.

options.label: Diamond
options.meaning: A diamond-type triply periodic surface pattern: a repeating curved three-dimensional structure, not ordinary diamond-shaped straight ribs.

options.label: TPMS-FK
options.meaning: The installed FK-named triply periodic surface option. It creates a repeating three-dimensional curved pattern; its exact parameterization is not established by the label.

options.label: Primitive
options.meaning: The Primitive-named triply periodic surface pattern, a repeating three-dimensional cell-and-connection geometry. It is distinct from adding a primitive model object.

options.label: Neovius
options.meaning: The Neovius-named triply periodic surface pattern. It offers a different repeating curved cell geometry; inspect channels and wall paths at the selected density.

options.label: Lidinoid
options.meaning: The Lidinoid-named triply periodic surface pattern. It offers another repeating curved three-dimensional geometry; density alone does not establish its strength.

options.label: Hilbert Curve
options.meaning: A winding, space-filling path with many right-angle turns. It produces a distinctive surface texture rather than a simple straight-line finish.

options.label: Archimedean Chords
options.meaning: A curved, spiral-derived fill layout. It changes the direction and visual texture of the fill; inspect the actual clipped paths.

options.label: Octagram Spiral
options.meaning: A star-like spiral fill layout. Its repeated turns give a distinctive path and surface pattern, not a guaranteed strength advantage.
